samir: FYI - urgent escalation from acct-4512. After we pinned them to a model during last night's maintenance, their embeddings index queries started failing with dimension mismatch. They reported production errors ~09:12 UTC.

olivia: ack. do we know which pinned model/version was applied?

samir: they were on model alias `embed-fast-2024` which we pinned to `embed-fast-2025-v2` (pin created at 2026-03-14T02:00Z). Customer expected 1536-dim vectors.

kai: got logs from their failed call: curl to /v1/embeddings -> 400 body:
```
{"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024 - index_account=acct-4512 index_name=kb_prod"}
```

support-bot: Incident auto-tag: escalation, embeddings, dimension-mismatch, priority=high :rotating_light:

olivia: interesting - we pushed a v2 model that's known to default to 1024 dims unless quant/arch mapping is applied. Did our pin mapping translate aliases to the correct variant?

samir: looking at the pin record now:
```
pin: {
  alias: "embed-fast-2024",
  pinned_to: "embed-fast-2025-v2",
  created_by: "infra-ops",
  created_at: "2026-03-14T02:00:13Z"
}
```

kai: runtime model metadata we return during load shows: `metadata.embedding_size=1024` for embed-fast-2025-v2 on the dedicated pool used by acct-4512. That would explain the mismatch.

olivia: does the model catalog entry for embed-fast-2025-v2 document a 1024 dimension?

samir: catalog: `embed-fast-2025-v2` had two published variants. One is `-dense-1024` (default tag) and another `-wide-1536` (opt-in). The alias translation pipeline accidentally resolved to the default variant because we removed the explicit variant tag when generating the pin during the deploy.

eng-oncall: any quick mitigation? Customer index queries are failing so they're seeing production errors.

kai: mitigation options:
- re-pin alias to the `-wide-1536` variant (requires a pin update; immediate routing change)
- re-run embedding ingestion against the new 1024 vectors and rebuild their index (non-trivial; breaks search semantics)
- add a compatibility shim to pad/trim vectors at runtime (unsafe and lossy)

olivia: re-pin seems safest for now. I'll prepare a pin rollback to point alias -> embed-fast-2025-v2-wide-1536 and push to the dedicated pool.

samir: customer confirms they want the original 1536 vectors. They've paused writes but still need reads working.

support-bot: deploy-bot: canary pin-change scheduled at 11:04 UTC. Logs will be posted.

kai: repro steps I used locally (dev cluster):
```
# request that shows vector length
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"embed-fast-2025-v2","input":"testing"}' | jq .data[0].embedding | length
# returns 1024
```

samir: customer stacktrace from their ingestion pipeline (abridged):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:40Z ERROR indexing: have_vector_dim=1536 expected_dim=1536 but got=1024 - embedding_length_mismatch
Trace: Indexer.validate_vector -> indexer.py:247
```

olivia: done. pin change applied and propagated to dedicated pool at 11:06 UTC. Can we confirm their reads are green?

eng-oncall: checking runtime logs for their tenant: after pin update we see model resolved to `embed-fast-2025-v2-wide-1536` and inference returns vectors with length 1536. No errors for 11:07-11:15 window.

samir: customer confirms tests passing again. They've resumed ingestion and will run a small reindex for docs that failed during the incident. They want a postmortem and that this not happen again.

olivia: root cause summary for PM: the pin generator used the alias string but dropped explicit variant suffix during a refactor; default resolution now points to the default variant (1024) instead of the previously targeted wide variant (1536). Fixes: 1) add variant tag enforcement in pin creation UI/CLI, 2) add pin validation that model.embedding_size == index.expected_dim with a warning blocker, 3) backfill existing pins to validate dimensions and notify affected customers.

kai: opened follow-up ticket SUP-1182 to add validation and SUP-1183 to run audit and notify customers.

samir: closing loop: customer satisfied, reindex in progress, support ticket updated with mitigation steps and timelines. Leaving this thread open for audit docs until SUP-1182 done. :white_check_mark:
